summary: Mikazuki Fields is a farmer-centered crop-rotation decision-support web app built like a 3-route GPS planner for a farmer's next six planting seasons (three years). To help farmers navigate shifting temperatures, irregular rainfall, water shortages, and declining soil health, we developed a tool that fuses 10 years of NASA POWER agroclimatology, SRTM 30m terrain slope, and MODIS MOD13Q1 250m NDVI bare-soil profiles into plain-English farm indicators. Combining these NASA Earth observations with local soil conditions (texture, pH, nitrogen, and flood history), FAO crop characteristics across eight crops, and farmer priorities (irrigation access, budget limits, staple needs, and water-soil-income sliders), our optimizer evaluates all 262,144 possible six-season rotations to compare Status Quo, Balanced Optimal, and Drought-Safe plans alongside an instant El Niño stress test (-25% rain, +1.5°C). This matters because turning complex satellite science into clear seasonal choices helps smallholder farmers break pest cycles, rebuild soil nitrogen, reduce slope erosion, conserve water, and protect yields and income before extreme weather hits.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mikazuki Fields is a crop-rotation planner for Philippine smallholder farms, built like a GPS that shows three routes for the next six planting seasons (three years). A farmer locates their farm, and the app compares a Status Quo, a Balanced Optimal, and a Drought-Safe rotation—showing for each one 3-year net profit, soil nitrogen balance, erosion risk, water demand, and pest-cycle breaks, alongside local Philippine crop varieties.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Find your farm: search a town, drop a pin, or trace the field's corners to get its size in hectares. Taps on water are refused.

2. Read the site: 10 years of NASA POWER climate (2015 to 2024), SRTM 30 m altitude and slope, MODIS NDVI green cover, and NASA GIBS satellite imagery, each labelled live or from a reference site.

3. Describe the field: soil texture and tests, water access, goal, budget, staple needs, last harvest and crops to exclude.

4. Compare routes: a NumPy optimizer tests all 262,144 six-season rotations of eight crops and returns the three best, with recommended Philippine varieties.

5. Stress-test and export: replay the farm's real 2015 to 2016 El Niño months, walk the six seasons on a 3D field, and download a PDF field report.

HOW THE DATA & CORE MATH WORK

- NASA POWER (2015–2024 rainfall, T2M, T2M_MAX, root-zone wetness GWETROOT, and solar radiation): Computes monthly reference water demand (ET0 = 0.0135 × (T2m + 17.8) × 0.408 × Solar), triggers heat-stress yield loss above each crop's temperature limit, penalizes waterlogging when GWETROOT > 0.85 (with 1.5× stronger penalties for root/tuber crops like sweet potato and peanut on heavy soils), favors short-cycle legumes (≤ 75 days) in dry rainfed seasons (< 350 mm), and supplies real 2015–2016 El Niño weather.

- NASA SRTM 30 m Terrain: Computes terrain slope (%) around the farm to drive seasonal soil erosion and block lowland paddy rice on steep uplands (slope > 8%).

- NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI & NASA GIBS WMTS: MOD13Q1 flags historical bare-soil months (NDVI < 0.30), infers starting soil nitrogen when untested (55–70 kg/ha), and increases dry-season erosion risk when vegetation cover is low (mean NDVI < 0.35). Live GIBS tiles (MODIS_Terra_NDVI_8Day and IMERG_Precipitation_Rate) let farmers visually inspect vegetation greenness and rainfall over their field.

- Water, Soil, Pest & Profit Physics (FAO-56/33 & PSA OpenSTAT): Each crop runs through a month-by-month soil bucket water balance. Rainfed shortfalls reduce yield via FAO-33 (YieldLoss = min(0.85, Ky × Gap / Demand)), while irrigated gaps convert to pumping cost (PHP 35/mm). Nitrogen carryover adds legume N fixation (halved if pH < 5.5) or charges urea top-up below 60 kg/ha; switching crop families cuts pest pressure (× 0.30) while repeating families compounds it (+0.25); and bare-field erosion follows Erosion = clip((Rain / 1200) × K_soil × (1 + Slope / 10) × CoverFactor × 50 × NDVI_mult, 0, 100).

- Profit & Route Selection: Seasonal profit is Profit = (EffectiveYield × FarmgatePrice) − CropCost − UreaCost − PumpCost (scaling Status Quo to the farmer's last harvest yield when provided). The optimizer normalizes Water, Soil (plus 3-family diversity bonuses), and Economy scores (penalizing losing seasons): Plan B maximizes 0.85 × NormalScore + 0.15 × ElNiñoScore under user priority sliders while avoiding back-to-back identical crops and 3-season same-family streaks, and Plan C excludes high-water rice crops to maximize worst-case Normal vs. El Niño resilience.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Farmers see before planting which rotation rebuilds soil nitrogen, breaks pest cycles, cuts erosion on slopes and still pays in a dry year. We want satellite data to reach the people who make the planting decision, in plain language and pesos, so a drought or a tired field costs less income.

TOOLS

- Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Three.js, and jsPDF.

- Backend & Data Science: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, NumPy, pandas, and pytest (deployable on Vercel).

- Datasets & Services: NASA POWER, NASA SRTM 30 m (via OpenTopoData), NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 (via ORNL DAAC), NASA GIBS WMTS, Open-Meteo, PSA OpenSTAT farmgate prices/yields, FAO crop coefficients, OpenStreetMap, Nominatim, and Esri World Imagery.

- Hardware: Developed on standard laptops and runs in any standard mobile phone, tablet, or desktop browser with no special hardware required.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Instead of a dense dashboard of scientific charts, the farmer pilots a cockpit view that descends onto their own field, and their selected 6-season rotation grows across seasons in an interactive 3D plot. El Niño stress testing replays actual 2015–2016 satellite-observed drought months rather than an abstract percentage, showing clearly why each crop succeeded or suffered.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Rural connectivity: Automatic fallback to pre-cached benchmark presets, an offline bundle, and an identical in-browser TypeScript Web Worker optimizer so the tool works even with unstable internet.

- Accessibility & trust: Mobile-friendly cockpit layout, plain-English tooltips, honest Live vs. Cached badges, a built-in "Know the limits" disclosure explaining satellite pixel resolution (~50–70 km POWER grid / 250 m MODIS), local PSA prices and Philippine crop varieties, and guidance to confirm switching plans with a DA soil lab test and the local Municipal Agriculturist.
